# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  Conformance claims are the self-certification blind spot (gh-1834):
  when the final claim includes parity/conformance to a reference or
  specification (any domain), a "verified" item counts only with
  negative and combination checks — refused incompatible options,
  empty/corrupt inputs, boundary values, must-NOT-work cases — alongside
  happy paths; a blanket "everything matches" is not verified (prompt
  step 2.6, conditional: tasks with no conformance claim are
  unchanged).
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). gh-1835: a foreground bash call still
  running after `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` (default 60; 0 = kill
  switch) is auto-backgrounded — CONVERTED, never restarted (it already
  runs as a registry job under the soft-yield path): the pending tool call
  resolves exactly once with the backgrounded result (`bash_auto_background
  .dart` text, anchored on the hand-back sentence so the loop's stuck
  supervisor and budget ladder classify it as a real conversion), the
  settle notification stays armed, an explicit `timeout` at/below the
  threshold keeps the classic path while one above carries over as the
  job's cap, and hosts without `BackgroundShell` keep legacy behavior.
  Headless `fa -p` DRAINS live shell
  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =
  shell-job-scoped kill switch: live shell jobs detach at once while the
  pre-existing subagent drain stays unconditional), then the detach
  summary applies (gh-1459). The drain wrap-up also raises the
  settle→reaction fence: from `_finishHeadlessDrain` on, a job settle (or
  task completion) does bookkeeping only — no reaction run (gh-1589 I2).
  While the drain waits, every `headless.shellJobQuietMs`
  (default 5 min; 0 = off) of a still-running awaited job steers ONE
  interim liveness notice (`job <id> running · <elapsed> · tail: …` +
  the bash_job escape hatch), skipped for a crossing the model probed
  itself (`bash_job status/output` bumps the entry's probe generation)
  (gh-1459 ask #4). The headless `finally` then closes the session with
  the SEAL (`Session.seal`, gh-1589): after the usage fold + the
  job-board/obligations/subagent flushes (close order: drain → usage
  fold → seal → exit, the REPL teardown seals the same way), every writer
  observes the sealed session — late appends are DROPPED with one stderr
  warning per writer class, never written, so the session JSONL is a
  sealed artifact before the process exits. The seal is per-run state
  (a resume opens the same file unsealed); the harbor adapter mirrors the
  contract from the outside: `run()` returns only after the fa process
  exited (kill + bounded reap on every path, incl. external cancel; loud
  degradation when the reap times out). Job logs on disk are NOT
  secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard

  subagents, other Fa instances sharing the root) owns a file inbox behind

  future DB/network impls drop in without caller changes).
  `AgentMessage.kind` distinguishes agent chat from `user` input handed
  over by an attached client (the Fa app's attach view; the CLI delivers
  it as `[from app] …`, its own words, not agent chat).

  agent dirs, torn writes skipped. `SubagentManager.messaging` routes

  the no-fabric fallback); `mailboxPrefix` (the session id, set by the host

  `agent_message` targets siblings, `main`, a session name, or an
  absolute mailbox; `agent_directory` lists LIVE fabric mailboxes (recent
  activity via the heartbeat hosts touch on their inbox-watch timers) plus
  anything with pending mail — stale mailboxes from finished sessions are
  hidden behind the tool's `all: true` (`.id` markers keep real ids despite
  dir sanitization; `_scheduled`/dot-dirs are not mailboxes).
  `schedule_message` (issue #59): records under `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/`;
  self-addressed records deliver to the host's LIVE mailbox at fire time
  (the address pinned at schedule time goes stale on session switch/restart
  and would strand the reminder) — EXCEPT self-addressed records naming a
  subagent mailbox of this session (`<prefix>/<childId>`, gh-970): those
  deliver as recorded (the address rides the same owner prefix and is as
  stable; re-addressing stole the child's reminder into main), and the
  tool's `senderMailbox` override (host-wired from `activeSubagentId()`)
  makes a subagent's no-`to` schedule default to the CHILD's mailbox, not
  main's — hosts re-arm on every mailbox change
  (CLI `_syncMailboxPrefix`, app `_setMailboxPrefix`) and sweep due records
  on their inbox ticks; `dispose()` cancels only the timer, the files stay.
  gh-1180: a re-addressed SELF record also delivers FROM the live mailbox
  (`from` rewritten alongside `to` in `_deliverDueInner`) — an adopted
  reminder keeps the self shape (from == to) the wake policy needs to
  classify it exempt, so a chain survives a session-id change. Every
  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.
  UI: `/agents` rows show a `mail:N` pending marker (the CLI
  font has no ✉ glyph), the app's AgentsSection shows `✉N`; observe/detail
  views list the pending inbox.

# gh-1825: [GOAL] /network + headless DAP: scoped channel joins, passphrase-encrypted keys (Keychain once / CI env), identity = session name

## Description

## Goal — `/network` + headless DAP provisioning: scoped channel membership (v3 — passphrase-encrypted channel keys + Keychain)

One sentence: **joining a DAP hub channel from the TUI takes three keystrokes** — `/network`, paste the invite, pick a scope — and from then on the agent receives (and can answer) channel traffic with the same steering semantics as peer mail, at exactly the chosen blast radius: this session, this project folder, or every agent on the machine.

Today joining is a shell-side `fa dap import` + config file + restart, with only GLOBAL membership (`~/.dap/config.json` channels). The owner's actual flow — copy the app's add-agent invite, get THIS agent (or this folder's agents) onto the channel — has no UI. This card builds it, on the existing DAP/1 fabric, no protocol changes.

## Why this framing

- Retracted framing: «paste the invite into the agent's chat message» — chat is not a command channel; the import is a CLI action (with an optional composer-paste shortcut, AC7, that turns the paste into the same join wizard instead of a dead end).
- Owner decision (2026-10-24): inbound channel messages get **full steering** — same as `agent_message` peer mail today. Not notify-only, not @mention-gated. The security section prices this in.

## UX (the core of the card)

`/network` opens a compact TUI menu:

1. **Join channel** (default row): a single paste field accepting EVERY reasonable form — `wss://hub.fa1.dev/ws?channel=<id>`, the same with `#pub=P&priv=K`, a bare `<channel-id>` (uses the configured hub), or the whole copied `fa dap import '…'` command line. One parser, one code path (extend `lib/src/hub/dap_invite_import.dart`, never a second regex).
   Next and only question: **scope — `(s)ession` / `(p)roject` / `(g)lobal`**, default `session`, single key. Join takes effect IMMEDIATELY (no restart): subscribe on the live hub connection (or connect on demand), first inbound frame can steer the very next turn.
2. **Channels**: joined channels with scope badges (`session`/`project`/`global`), live/offline hub state, per-channel `leave` (stops delivery + unsubscribes + removes the stored membership at that scope) and `copy invite` (private channels only when the keypair is present; the invite string matches what the Fa app produces, so app↔CLI invites are symmetric).
3. **Status**: hub url, connection state, reconnect action (the existing `dap_connect` machinery).

Full flow: `/network` → Enter → paste → Enter → `s` (or Enter for the default) → joined. No shell, no restart, no file editing.

## Architecture

- **Membership stores, by scope** (one record shape everywhere: `{hubUrl, channelId, pub?, priv?, joinedAt}`):
  - `session` — a `dap_channel_membership` custom record on the session JSONL tree: survives resume (replay re-joins), dies with the branch; only this session's agent.
  - `project` — `.fah/dap.json` in the project root (MUST be gitignored, see secrets): every fa agent booted from that folder on this machine joins at startup.
  - `global` — the existing `~/.dap/config.json` channel list: unchanged mechanism, all agents on the machine.
- **Effective membership = union(session, project, global)**, deduped by `(hubUrl, channelId)`: joining the same channel at two scopes delivers each frame ONCE (dedup by message id at the existing fabric drain; leave at one scope keeps the other).
- **Delivery**: inbound channel frames ride the SAME `externalSteeringSource` drain as peer mail (turn boundaries + idle wake), provenance-prefixed (`#channel · sender`). Outbound: the agent writes with the existing `agent_message to: "#channel"` fabric path — no new tool; the TUI human can also type into the channel from the `/network` menu.
- Existing invariants stand: subagent drains never touch the hub; hub down → file-fabric fallback + reconnect with backoff; `fa dap import` keeps working (it is the global-scope import, now one of three scopes).

## Capability surface

Core: join (all invite forms, 3 scopes, live effect), list, leave, copy invite, status/reconnect, inbound steering, outbound write, resume/reboot re-join per scope, cross-scope dedup, composer-paste shortcut (AC7).
Second tier (follow-up friendly, not this card): `/network create` (mint channel + show invite for the app), per-channel mute, unread counters in the TUI chrome.
Excluded (rationale): no LAN listener/pairing work (separate card); no channel-admin/moderation concepts (DAP/1 has none); no auto-reply/bot mode (the agent answers when it decides, not on every frame); no committed PLAINTEXT key material (v3: committed config with passphrase-ENCRYPTED keys is allowed and is the CI path — see Security).

## Security & secrets

- **Trust model**: a joined channel is a shared trust domain — by the owner's full-steering decision, ANY member (app, other agents, anyone with the invite) can steer this agent. The join UI must say so in one line (`members can steer this agent`), and scope is the blast-radius control: session < project < global. Provenance prefix on every steered frame is mandatory (the human can always see WHERE an instruction came from).
- **Where the channel secret lives (owner decision, v3)**: the channel config JSON holds the private key ONLY in passphrase-encrypted form (KDF + AEAD, built on the existing `lib/src/messaging/hub_crypto.dart` primitives, versioned envelope `dapkey1`). Plaintext `priv` exists only in memory — and in the pure-env CI path, where the secret store IS the protection.
  | surface | channel config (encrypted keys) | passphrase |
  |---|---|---|
  | global | `~/.dap/channels.json` (encrypted entries) | OS Keychain, else one prompt |
  | project scope | `.fah/dap.json` — MAY be committed to git (encrypted keys only; this RETRACTS the v1/v2 gitignore-only stance: encrypted-at-rest makes a committed, team-shared channel list safe, and it is exactly what CI needs) | OS Keychain per machine, or `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` from CI secrets |
  | session scope | `dap_channel_membership` record in the session JSONL, keys encrypted the same way | same resolution chain |
  | headless/CI | the same JSON (checked out from the repo or injected via `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON`) | `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` env secret; NO prompts ever |
- **Passphrase resolution chain (per channel, in this order)**: (1) `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` env (CI); (2) OS Keychain item — **unique per channel: `fa.dap.channel-key.<hubHost>.<channelId>`** (many channels, zero name conflicts; hub host included so the same channel id on two hubs never collides); (3) interactive prompt ONCE with save-to-Keychain as the default. After that, every new session from that folder joins the channel silently.
- **Keychain platform matrix**: macOS Keychain first-class (this card). Linux CI uses the env path (no keychain dependency). Linux Secret Service / Windows DPAPI storage backends = second tier, behind the same `ChannelKeyStore` interface — the resolution chain and UX do not change, only the backend. No keychain backend AND no env on a headless run → loud one-line warning + the agent's primary job proceeds (never a prompt, never a block).
- **Pure-env alternative (must keep working)**: `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` entries may carry PLAINTEXT `priv` straight from the CI secret store — no passphrase, no keychain, no encrypted envelope required. Both modes are first-class; mixed (some channels encrypted, some plaintext-env) is allowed.
- Channel keypairs (`priv`) are credentials: project store and session-record serialization MUST be covered by `.gitignore` and the existing redaction pipeline; never logged, never echoed (the `runDapImport` I2 rule), never rendered into outbound model context beyond the already-established invite handling. Test: byte-scan of `git status`-visible files and of a serialized session record containing a private-key membership; CI test: the env values never appear in any session JSONL/tool result (redactor registered for them, the `SessionKeysStore` pattern).
- Hub url scheme is preserved end-to-end (`wss://` stays TLS; no downgrade to `ws://` except the loopback dev default).

## Headless / CI-CD provisioning (owner requirement, v2)

An agent started by CI (e.g. the machine's **ai-teammate** on issue assignment, new session or resume) must join the team's channel with ZERO interactive steps and be steerable/report-back-able immediately:

- **Env contract** (all optional, all zero-prompt; names are the NEW headless surface, documented in `docs/dap.md`):
  - `DAP_HUB_URL` — e.g. `wss://hub.fa1.dev/ws` (GitHub secret).
  - `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET` — the hub-issued per-client secret (GitHub secret); enrollment via `DAP_MASTER_SECRET` stays the interactive path and is never required on CI.
  - `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` — passphrase for encrypted channel keys (GitHub secret); consulted before Keychain, never prompted for.
  - `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` — `[{"channel":"<id>","pub":"…","priv":"…"}, …]` (GitHub secret; keyless entries for public channels; entries may be encrypted envelopes (decrypted with `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`) or plaintext-priv straight from the secret store). These join AT BOOT, before the first turn, exactly like a global-scope membership but with no `$HOME` dependency.
- **Identity = session name**: when the CLI runs with `--session <name>` (the ai-teammate convention), the agent's hub display name IS the session name, automatically — no separate naming step, stable across resumes, so `agent_directory`/channel presence shows `ai-teammate`'s session by its familiar name and `agent_message to: "<session-name>"` resolves. Without a session name the current generated-identity behavior stays.
- **Headless steering**: inbound channel frames ride the same external-inbox drain in headless runs (mid-run steering + between-run idle wake); outbound `agent_message to: "#channel"` works identically, so the agent can post progress/results to the channel. The existing headless drain/seal ordering (shell jobs, subagents) is unchanged.
- **Failure policy on CI**: hub unreachable or secret rejected → the agent still runs its primary job (bench/issue work) with a loud one-line warning; DAP is never a hard dependency of the primary task. File-fabric fallback unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Join-by-paste works for all four invite forms (url, url+keys, bare id, full `fa dap import '…'` command) and takes effect without restart: a frame sent to the channel right after the join steers the agent's next turn. (IT-1..4, E2E-1)
- **AC2** — Scope semantics: session membership is invisible to a second CLI in the same folder; project membership joins every agent booted from that folder (and not from a sibling folder); global joins all agents on the machine. (IT-2, E2E-2)
- **AC3** — Resume/reboot: session membership re-joins after `fa --session` resume; project/global re-join on every boot. (IT-3, E2E-3)
- **AC4** — Union + dedup: the same channel joined at two scopes delivers one frame once; leaving one scope keeps the other alive; leaving the last scope stops delivery. (IT-4)
- **AC5** — Write path: `agent_message to: "#channel"` from the agent and the menu's send box both land in the channel and are visible to the Fa app. (E2E-4)
- **AC6** — `/network` full flow is ≤5 keystrokes past the paste; the menu lists scope badges and live hub state. (E2E-5, TUI golden)
- **AC7** — Pasting a DAP invite into the normal composer opens the SAME join wizard (with the pasted value prefilled) instead of sending it as an agent message. (UT-5, E2E-6)
- **AC8** — Secrets: no private key bytes in any git-visible file, log, or tool result; join UI shows the steering trust notice. (UT-6 + byte-scan)
- **AC9** — Hub down at join: clear error, membership stored anyway, auto-join on reconnect; existing file-fabric fallback unaffected. (IT-5)

- **AC10** — Headless env-only boot: with `DAP_HUB_URL` + `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET` + `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` set (and an EMPTY `$HOME` DAP config), `fa -p` joins the channel before the first turn, receives steering, and can post back; zero prompts, zero writes outside a temp DAP home. (IT-6, E2E-7)
- **AC11** — Identity: `--session goal_builder` → the hub display name is `goal_builder` (visible in presence/`agent_directory`, addressable by name); resume keeps it. (IT-7, E2E-8)
- **AC12** — The ai-teammate flow end-to-end: an assigned issue starts (or resumes) a CI session with the env secrets configured → the agent appears in the channel by its session name → a channel message steers it mid-run → its `agent_message` answer lands in the channel. Hub down → primary job still completes with a warning. (E2E-9)

- **AC13** — Passphrase once, then silent: first join with an encrypted key prompts once (default: save to Keychain); EVERY later session from that folder joins with no prompt. Keychain items are per-channel unique (`fa.dap.channel-key.<hubHost>.<channelId>`): 20 channels on 2 hubs = 20 distinct items, no overwrite. (IT-8 with a fake ChannelKeyStore, E2E-10 on macOS Keychain)
- **AC14** — CI passphrase path: a committed `.fah/dap.json` with encrypted keys + `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` from GitHub secrets joins headlessly with no keychain and no prompts; the passphrase never lands in session JSONL/tool results (redactor registered). A committed-config test byte-scans the repo-visible JSON for plaintext key material. (IT-9, E2E-11)
- **AC15** — Pure-env path: plaintext `priv` in `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` works with no passphrase and no Keychain; mixed encrypted+plaintext channel sets join together. Wrong passphrase → clear error + primary job proceeds, never a retry-loop block. (IT-10, E2E-12)

## Test plan

- `UT-1..6`: invite parser (all forms incl. pasted command, garbage rejection), membership record (de)serialization, scope-union/dedup logic, composer-paste detector, secret byte-scans. Pure Dart, no IO.
- `IT-1..10`: FakeHub (`test/hub/fake_hub.dart`) — join/steer/leave per scope, resume replay, reconnect, dedup across scopes.
- `E2E-1..12`: real CLI + `fa hub serve` + an app-produced invite string (fixture from the Fa app) — join, steer, write, resume, TUI golden of the menu; E2E-7/8/9: headless env boot on a clean `$HOME`, session-name identity, the ai-teammate-style assign→join→steer→report loop; E2E-10: real macOS Keychain once-then-silent; E2E-11/12: CI passphrase and pure-env boots.
- `REG-*`: the whole existing DAP suite stays green; semantic-drift check: `fa dap import` (old path) and `/network` global join (new path) produce byte-equivalent effective membership. A red REG job blocks merge even when all new tests are green.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Same channel at session+global: single delivery; leave(session) keeps global.
- **E2** — Kill mid-join: no half-written membership record (atomic write); resume either joins fully or not at all.
- **E3** — Invite for a DIFFERENT hub than configured: join stores per-channel hub url (never clobbers the default hub config — the existing `runDapImport` no-clobber rule).
- **E4** — Garbage/non-invite paste: inline validation error, nothing stored, no message sent to the agent.
- **E5** — Session fork/branch: membership follows the branch it was recorded on; navigating to a branch without the record unsubscribes.
- **E6** — Private-channel invite with keys: `copy invite` reproduces a working invite (round-trip through the parser); keyless/public channel: copy produces the keyless form.

## Non-goals

No DAP/1 protocol changes; no interactive enrollment on CI (per-client secrets only); no LAN listener/pairing; no channel creation UI (second tier); no committed PLAINTEXT keys (committed ENCRYPTED config is v3 core); no auto-reply mode; no changes to the file-fabric fallback.

## Open questions

None blocking — full-steering decided by the owner. (Second-tier candidates to groom later: `/network create`, mute, unread badges.)

## References

`docs/dap.md` (§8.1 hub bring-up, §12 fabric, §13 app agents), `bin/fah_dap_command.dart` `runDapImport` (invite import + no-clobber rule), `lib/src/hub/dap_invite_import.dart` (parser to extend), `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart` (`dap_*` tools, externalSteeringSource), `lib/src/messaging/` (fabric + fallback), owner flow that motivated this: `fa dap import 'wss://hub.fa1.dev/ws?channel=…'` had no TUI path.

- Existing invariants stand: subagent drains never touch the hub; hub down → file-fabric fallback + reconnect with backoff; `fa dap import` keeps working (it is the global-scope import, now one of three scopes).

## Capability surface

Core: join (all invite forms, 3 scopes, live effect), list, leave, copy invite, status/reconnect, inbound steering, outbound write, resume/reboot re-join per scope, cross-scope dedup, composer-paste shortcut (AC7).
Second tier (follow-up friendly, not this card): `/network create` (mint channel + show invite for the app), per-channel mute, unread counters in the TUI chrome.
Excluded (rationale): no LAN listener/pairing work (separate card); no channel-admin/moderation concepts (DAP/1 has none); no auto-reply/bot mode (the agent answers when it decides, not on every frame); no committed PLAINTEXT key material (v3: committed config with passphrase-ENCRYPTED keys is allowed and is the CI path — see Security).

## Security & secrets

- **Trust model**: a joined channel is a shared trust domain — by the owner's full-steering decision, ANY member (app, other agents, anyone with the invite) can steer this agent. The join UI must say so in one line (`members can steer this agent`), and scope is the blast-radius control: session < project < global. Provenance prefix on every steered frame is mandatory (the human can always see WHERE an instruction came from).
- **Where the channel secret lives (owner decision, v3)**: the channel config JSON holds the private key ONLY in passphrase-encrypted form (KDF + AEAD, built on the existing `lib/src/messaging/hub_crypto.dart` primitives, versioned envelope `dapkey1`). Plaintext `priv` exists only in memory — and in the pure-env CI path, where the secret store IS the protection.
  | surface | channel config (encrypted keys) | passphrase |
  |---|---|---|
  | global | `~/.dap/channels.json` (encrypted entries) | OS Keychain, else one prompt |
  | project scope | `.fah/dap.json` — MAY be committed to git (encrypted keys only; this RETRACTS the v1/v2 gitignore-only stance: encrypted-at-rest makes a committed, team-shared channel list safe, and it is exactly what CI needs) | OS Keychain per machine, or `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` from CI secrets |
  | session scope | `dap_channel_membership` record in the session JSONL, keys encrypted the same way | same resolution chain |
  | headless/CI | the same JSON (checked out from the repo or injected via `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON`) | `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` env secret; NO prompts ever |
- **Passphrase resolution chain (per channel, in this order)**: (1) `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` env (CI); (2) OS Keychain item — **unique per channel: `fa.dap.channel-key.<hubHost>.<channelId>`** (many channels, zero name conflicts; hub host included so the same channel id on two hubs never collides); (3) interactive prompt ONCE with save-to-Keychain as the default. After that, every new session from that folder joins the channel silently.
- **Keychain platform matrix**: macOS Keychain first-class (this card). Linux CI uses the env path (no keychain dependency). Linux Secret Service / Windows DPAPI storage backends = second tier, behind the same `ChannelKeyStore` interface — the resolution chain and UX do not change, only the backend. No keychain backend AND no env on a headless run → loud one-line warning + the agent's primary job proceeds (never a prompt, never a block).
- **Pure-env alternative (must keep working)**: `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` entries may carry PLAINTEXT `priv` straight from the CI secret store — no passphrase, no keychain, no encrypted envelope required. Both modes are first-class; mixed (some channels encrypted, some plaintext-env) is allowed.
- Channel keypairs (`priv`) are credentials: project store and session-record serialization MUST be covered by `.gitignore` and the existing redaction pipeline; never logged, never echoed (the `runDapImport` I2 rule), never rendered into outbound model context beyond the already-established invite handling. Test: byte-scan of `git status`-visible files and of a serialized session record containing a private-key membership; CI test: the env values never appear in any session JSONL/tool result (redactor registered for them, the `SessionKeysStore` pattern).
- Hub url scheme is preserved end-to-end (`wss://` stays TLS; no downgrade to `ws://` except the loopback dev default).

## Headless / CI-CD provisioning (owner requirement, v2)

An agent started by CI (e.g. the machine's **ai-teammate** on issue assignment, new session or resume) must join the team's channel with ZERO interactive steps and be steerable/report-back-able immediately:

- **Env contract** (all optional, all zero-prompt; names are the NEW headless surface, documented in `docs/dap.md`):
  - `DAP_HUB_URL` — e.g. `wss://hub.fa1.dev/ws` (GitHub secret).
  - `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET` — the hub-issued per-client secret (GitHub secret); enrollment via `DAP_MASTER_SECRET` stays the interactive path and is never required on CI.
  - `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` — passphrase for encrypted channel keys (GitHub secret); consulted before Keychain, never prompted for.
  - `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` — `[{"channel":"<id>","pub":"…","priv":"…"}, …]` (GitHub secret; keyless entries for public channels; entries may be encrypted envelopes (decrypted with `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`) or plaintext-priv straight from the secret store). These join AT BOOT, before the first turn, exactly like a global-scope membership but with no `$HOME` dependency.
- **Identity = session name**: when the CLI runs with `--session <name>` (the ai-teammate convention), the agent's hub display name IS the session name, automatically — no separate naming step, stable across resumes, so `agent_directory`/channel presence shows `ai-teammate`'s session by its familiar name and `agent_message to: "<session-name>"` resolves. Without a session name the current generated-identity behavior stays.
- **Headless steering**: inbound channel frames ride the same external-inbox drain in headless runs (mid-run steering + between-run idle wake); outbound `agent_message to: "#channel"` works identically, so the agent can post progress/results to the channel. The existing headless drain/seal ordering (shell jobs, subagents) is unchanged.
- **Failure policy on CI**: hub unreachable or secret rejected → the agent still runs its primary job (bench/issue work) with a loud one-line warning; DAP is never a hard dependency of the primary task. File-fabric fallback unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Join-by-paste works for all four invite forms (url, url+keys, bare id, full `fa dap import '…'` command) and takes effect without restart: a frame sent to the channel right after the join steers the agent's next turn. (IT-1..4, E2E-1)
- **AC2** — Scope semantics: session membership is invisible to a second CLI in the same folder; project membership joins every agent booted from that folder (and not from a sibling folder); global joins all agents on the machine. (IT-2, E2E-2)
- **AC3** — Resume/reboot: session membership re-joins after `fa --session` resume; project/global re-join on every boot. (IT-3, E2E-3)
- **AC4** — Union + dedup: the same channel joined at two scopes delivers one frame once; leaving one scope keeps the other alive; leaving the last scope stops delivery. (IT-4)
- **AC5** — Write path: `agent_message to: "#channel"` from the agent and the menu's send box both land in the channel and are visible to the Fa app. (E2E-4)
- **AC6** — `/network` full flow is ≤5 keystrokes past the paste; the menu lists scope badges and live hub state. (E2E-5, TUI golden)
- **AC7** — Pasting a DAP invite into the normal composer opens the SAME join wizard (with the pasted value prefilled) instead of sending it as an agent message. (UT-5, E2E-6)
- **AC8** — Secrets: no private key bytes in any git-visible file, log, or tool result; join UI shows the steering trust notice. (UT-6 + byte-scan)
- **AC9** — Hub down at join: clear error, membership stored anyway, auto-join on reconnect; existing file-fabric fallback unaffected. (IT-5)

- **AC10** — Headless env-only boot: with `DAP_HUB_URL` + `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET` + `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` set (and an EMPTY `$HOME` DAP config), `fa -p` joins the channel before the first turn, receives steering, and can post back; zero prompts, zero writes outside a temp DAP home. (IT-6, E2E-7)
- **AC11** — Identity: `--session goal_builder` → the hub display name is `goal_builder` (visible in presence/`agent_directory`, addressable by name); resume keeps it. (IT-7, E2E-8)
- **AC12** — The ai-teammate flow end-to-end: an assigned issue starts (or resumes) a CI session with the env secrets configured → the agent appears in the channel by its session name → a channel message steers it mid-run → its `agent_message` answer lands in the channel. Hub down → primary job still completes with a warning. (E2E-9)

- **AC13** — Passphrase once, then silent: first join with an encrypted key prompts once (default: save to Keychain); EVERY later session from that folder joins with no prompt. Keychain items are per-channel unique (`fa.dap.channel-key.<hubHost>.<channelId>`): 20 channels on 2 hubs = 20 distinct items, no overwrite. (IT-8 with a fake ChannelKeyStore, E2E-10 on macOS Keychain)
- **AC14** — CI passphrase path: a committed `.fah/dap.json` with encrypted keys + `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` from GitHub secrets joins headlessly with no keychain and no prompts; the passphrase never lands in session JSONL/tool results (redactor registered). A committed-config test byte-scans the repo-visible JSON for plaintext key material. (IT-9, E2E-11)
- **AC15** — Pure-env path: plaintext `priv` in `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` works with no passphrase and no Keychain; mixed encrypted+plaintext channel sets join together. Wrong passphrase → clear error + primary job proceeds, never a retry-loop block. (IT-10, E2E-12)

## Test plan

- `UT-1..6`: invite parser (all forms incl. pasted command, garbage rejection), membership record (de)serialization, scope-union/dedup logic, composer-paste detector, secret byte-scans. Pure Dart, no IO.
- `IT-1..10`: FakeHub (`test/hub/fake_hub.dart`) — join/steer/leave per scope, resume replay, reconnect, dedup across scopes.
- `E2E-1..12`: real CLI + `fa hub serve` + an app-produced invite string (fixture from the Fa app) — join, steer, write, resume, TUI golden of the menu; E2E-7/8/9: headless env boot on a clean `$HOME`, session-name identity, the ai-teammate-style assign→join→steer→report loop; E2E-10: real macOS Keychain once-then-silent; E2E-11/12: CI passphrase and pure-env boots.
- `REG-*`: the whole existing DAP suite stays green; semantic-drift check: `fa dap import` (old path) and `/network` global join (new path) produce byte-equivalent effective membership. A red REG job blocks merge even when all new tests are green.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Same channel at session+global: single delivery; leave(session) keeps global.
- **E2** — Kill mid-join: no half-written membership record (atomic write); resume either joins fully or not at all.
- **E3** — Invite for a DIFFERENT hub than configured: join stores per-channel hub url (never clobbers the default hub config — the existing `runDapImport` no-clobber rule).
- **E4** — Garbage/non-invite paste: inline validation error, nothing stored, no message sent to the agent.
- **E5** — Session fork/branch: membership follows the branch it was recorded on; navigating to a branch without the record unsubscribes.
- **E6** — Private-channel invite with keys: `copy invite` reproduces a working invite (round-trip through the parser); keyless/public channel: copy produces the keyless form.

## Non-goals

No DAP/1 protocol changes; no interactive enrollment on CI (per-client secrets only); no LAN listener/pairing; no channel creation UI (second tier); no committed PLAINTEXT keys (committed ENCRYPTED config is v3 core); no auto-reply mode; no changes to the file-fabric fallback.

## Open questions

None blocking — full-steering decided by the owner. (Second-tier candidates to groom later: `/network create`, mute, unread badges.)

The drain path looks reasonable: `_steringLine` in agent_cli_inbox.dart adds provenance ` in #channel` plus reply hint. But the ticket said provenance prefix `#channel · sender` — the implementation uses `[from $fromId in $channel]`. Close enough.

Wait — the `_steringLine` mention regex: `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])@${name}(?![A-Za-z0-9_])` case-insensitive. The ticket says "word-boundary — no email or @name2 false positives". Email-shaped x@name: left char is a word char `[A-Za-z0-9_]`? Email `x@name` — the char before `@` is `x`, a word char, so `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` fails... Actually the pattern requires the preceding char to be non-word or start. `x@name` → preceding char `x` is a word char → no match. Good.

Now let me check a couple of important areas:
1. The `acceptsChannel` filter passes `hubUrl ?? scoped.defaultHubUrl` as `_connectedHubUrl`. But membership hubUrl values were normalized via `normalizeHubUrl` (which strips the `channel=` query param). Is `_connectedHubUrl` normalized? In `_applyBootMembership`, `_connectedHubUrl = preferred.hubUrl` where preferred.hubUrl came from stored memberships (normalized). In `_ensureChannelConnection`, `_connectedHubUrl = normalized`. OK. But `_connectWithScopedBoot`: `_connectedHubUrl ??= scoped?.defaultHubUrl` — normalized. OK.

2. The leave tombstone: `_loadSession` reads records via `context.readSessionRecords` → `branch` records. Leave tombstone key: `'${data['hubUrl']}\n${data['channelId']}'`. Join records have normalized hubUrl. Leave records store `hubUrl` passed to `leave()` — from `_networkLeaveChannel` which presumably passes membership.hubUrl (normalized). OK.

3. In `_loadSession`, `byKey.remove('${data['hubUrl']}\n${data['channelId']}')` — if hubUrl in the leave record has different normalization than join, the tombstone misses. Minor.

Now, security review of the envelope: 
- PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 100k iterations — fine.
- AD = 'dapkey1' static — weak AD but acceptable since salt/nonce random.
- `decryptChannelPriv` — the `ct.sublist(ct.length - 16)` for MAC. `if (ct.length < 16) throw` — but ct must be >= 16 + plaintext; a ct of exactly 16 would give empty cipherText; Chacha20 decrypt of empty with valid MAC... edge case, fine.
- Envelope JSON `decoded['iter'] as int` — if iter is e.g. a huge number from a hostile envelope → PBKDF2 with huge iterations → DoS/hang. `Pbkdf2(iterations:)` — a malicious `.fah/dap.json` committed in a repo could specify `iter: 999` and hang the agent at boot. Is there a cap? Let me check: `_deriveKey` uses `iterations` directly from the envelope. No upper bound! A malicious committed `.fah/dap.json` (which the ticket explicitly says MAY be committed and thus can come from a git clone of an untrusted repo) with `iter: 1000` would hang CPU for a very long time at boot when the passphrase is available (env). That's a real DoS vector. PBKDF2 at 1e9 iterations ≈ hours. Even 1e7 iterations ~ minutes. Worth flaging as IMPORTANT (or BLOCKING?). It's a genuine unbounded-work input. I'd call it IMPORTANT (DoS via malicious committed config; requires the passphrase to be present). Hmm, actually with wrong/no passphrase the AEAD tag check happens after KDF, so the KDF cost is paid regardless. Since `.fah/dap.json` can be committed to a team repo, cloning an untrusted repo and running fa in it would trigger it only if DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE is set or the keychain has an item for that channel (unlikely for a random channel id). Actually the keychain item is per channel: `fa.dap.channel-key.<host>.<channelId>` — for a malicious random channel id, the keychain lookup would miss and headless would skip decryption... but env path (CI) has a global passphrase → decryption attempted → KDF with attacker-controlled iteration count runs. In CI the repo IS trusted typically. Still, an unbounded iteration count is a defect. Flag as IMPORTANT.

Wait, actually a real issue: in `_globalJoin`, when the invite contains priv, plaintext is persisted to the legacy global file. But the ticket says global scope = legacy `~/.dap/config.json` "unchanged mechanism". The v3 decision says "the channel config JSON holds the private key ONLY in passphrase-encrypted form" — with a table saying global scope = `~/.dap/channels.json` (encrypted entries)! Look at the ticket table:

| global | `~/.dap/channels.json` (encrypted entries) | OS Keychain, else one prompt |

But the implementation's `_globalJoin` writes PLAINTEXT priv via `client.persistChannelKeys(globalChannelsFile, ...)` for the global scope. That contradicts the ticket's v3 security table which says global channel config holds encrypted entries. Hmm — but REG-* requires byte-equivalence with `fa dap import`, and `fa dap import` (legacy) writes plaintext to `~/.dap/channels.json`. The CHANGELOG says "global keeps the legacy `~/.dap` files". The PR description says: "global keeps the legacy ~/.dap files". So the PR deliberately deviates from the ticket's table for the global scope to preserve the REG byte-equivalence. This is a deviation from the ticket's security table — the ticket says "global | ~/.dap/channels.json (encrypted entries)". The PR instead keeps plaintext for global-scope joins (same as today's `fa dap import`).

Is this a justified deviation? The ticket itself says "`fa dap import` keeps working (it is the global-scope import, now one of three scopes)" and REG requires byte-equivalence between `fa dap import` and `/network` global join. If `/network` global join encrypted the keys while `fa dap import` writes plaintext, the REG byte-equivalence test would fail unless the import also changed. Per the external-spec evidence rule I can cite ticket.md. Since the PR description acknowledges it ("global keeps the legacy ~/.dap files"), it's a deliberate decision — I'll raise it as IMPORTANT (needs explicit owner confirmation), not BLOCKING.

The fanet1 decode fallback for the app is in network_session.dart. The claim in the CHANGELOG about the CLI "inbound channel frames open fanet1 first" — the CLI lib-side HubMessagingRepository._onChannelMsg does NOT handle fanet1. But wait, maybe the vendored client (fa_hub_client 0.2.11) decodes fanet1 before frames reach the repository? No — HubMessagingRepository in lib/src/messaging IS this repo's own code that reads raw frames from HubSocket. `_onChannelMsg` tries: keys==null → public decode; else whois+hubDecryptPayloadWithKeyPair. If the app sends fanet1 (base64 of 0x01||spk||nonce||ct||tag), base64Decode succeeds, then `_deriveDmKey` with sender DH from whois, AEAD decrypt with ad `dap1|id|channel`... The fanet1 inner frame is exactly `nonce||ct||tag` with ad `dap1|frameId|channelId` — hubDecryptPayloadWithKeyPair does `raw.sublist(12, len-16)` as ciphertext, nonce = first 12 bytes, ad = `dap1|id|aadTarget`. The fanet1 frame's AEAD portion is exactly that! So decrypting a fanet1 frame as if it were a raw dap1 payload: raw = decoded fanet1 bytes = 1 + 32 + 12 + ct + 16. `hubDecryptPayloadWithKeyPair` takes nonce = raw[0..12) — which is 0x01 || spk[0..11] — WRONG nonce. So decrypt fails → "dropped undecryptable channel mail". 

Hmm wait — but the live verification claim: "private channel messages decrypted in both directions between a headless DAP agent and the Flutter app". The headless DAP agent uses the CLI plugin path with the VENDORED fa_hub_client 0.2.11 (bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart), not lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart. The vendored 0.2.11 client presumably opens fanet1 first (published package, not in this repo — can't verify). So the claim may hold for the vendored path.

But lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart is used by the CLI fabric (hub fabric repository, bin/hub_fabric_repository.dart) and by the app per AGENTS.md ("HubMessagingRepository.joinChannel/waitForConnection" harness additions). If the fabric path is active (`DAP_MASTER_SECRET` + hub plugin), inbound channel mail flows through lib's `_onChannelMsg` which cannot decode fanet1 frames from the app. The CHANGELOG says "Inbound channel frames open `fanet1` first and fall back to legacy `dap/1` payloads" — that claim is not implemented in lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart. Let me double check the diff of hub_messaging_repository.dart to see if there was fanet1 handling added and I missed it... The full current file is above: `_onChannelMsg` → keys==null ? public : whois+decrypt. No fanet1 detection (data[0]==1 && length > 61). So either the claim refers to the vendored client only, or it's a gap.

Given interop is a core ticket goal ("Interop with fa_network public payloads and self-describing private fanet1 frames via published fa_hub_client 0.2.11"), and lib's HubMessagingRepository is the fabric used by `fa serve --a2a`... hmm, actually let me check who uses HubMessagingRepository.joinChannel in this repo — flutter_app? grep.

Hmm wait, but let me be careful: maybe fa_hub_client 0.2.11's fanet1 is only used on the RECEIVE side claim and sends remain dap1 unless negotiated? The CHANGELOG: "DAP private-channel sends now use self-describing fanet1 frames (sender X25519 key in the frame, channel-bound AD) via fa_hub_client 0.2.11, so fa_network app members decrypt them without a whois/senderKey round-trip." So sends via fa_hub_client use fanet1 — the headless CLI agent uses fa_hub_client → sends fanet1 → the Fa app (per the changelog sentence, "fa_network app members") decrypt via EnvelopeCodec — that's the fa_network relay path (network_session), NOT the DAP hub path! The Fa app has two ways to be on a channel: (1) fa_network member via relay (network_session, EnvelopeCodec — handles fanet1), (2) DAP join via agent_network_controller (lib repository — no fanet1). The live verification was presumably path (1). For path (2), interop breaks.

Is path (2) in scope? Yes — the PR adds "Flutter app DAP enrollment ... channel chat" — dap_enrollment_service.dart joins channels via agent_network_controller. So the app CAN join a DAP channel via the DAP path, and a headless fa_hub_client 0.2.11 agent's private messages would be dropped. That's an important interop gap. I'll flag it as BLOCKING? or IMPORTANT? The behavior: messages silently dropped (with a debugPrint). The PR explicitly claims fanet1 interop; this path misses it. Given "when in doubt, start one level higher" and this is a correctness bug in a headline feature, I'll make it BLOCKING... 

Hmm, but consider: maybe the vendored client's fanet1 send includes the sender key AND falls back... no, on the receive side in lib there's no fallback. Let me also check test coverage — hub_messaging_frames_test.dart covers "PUBLIC channel mail" only. And is there a test for fanet1 inbound in lib? grep tests.

content.thinking:
OK so the CLI fabric send path uses fa_hub_client 0.2.11's `sendChannelFanet1`. The RECEIVE path (CLI) goes through the vendored package's HubMessagingRepository (`repo.drain('#channel')`) — the package "opens fanet1 first and falls back to legacy" per the CHANGELOG (presumably in 0.2.11; not in this repo).

Now the remaining gap: the pure-Dart lib's `HubMessagingRepository` (`lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart`) — used by the FLUTER APP (agent_network_controller) — does NOT handle fanet1 inbound. The app's DAP-enrollment channel chat would drop private-channel fanet1 frames from CLI agents. Let me verify how the app's DAP channel chat receives messages — via `_fileFabric` composite (primary = lib's HubMessagingRepository). So yes, inbound DAP channel mail in the app flows through lib's `_onChannelMsg`. If the CLI fabric sends fanet1 (which the new code in hub_fabric_repository.dart explicitly does — `sendChannelFanet1`!), then the app side drops it.

Wait, actually — let me check `_onChannelMsg` once more. A fanet1 frame payload = base64(0x01 || spk(32) || nonce(12) || ct || tag). `hubDecryptPayloadWithKeyPair`: raw.length >= 28 OK; ciphertext = raw[12 .. len-16] — includes spk tail + real ct; nonce = raw[0..12] = 0x01||spk[0..11]. AEAD fails → dropped. Confirmed gap.

But maybe the app's agent_network_controller path is for a DIFFERENT mode (fa_network DAP enrollment where the app itself acts as a DAP agent on the hub). If both CLI and app are on the hub: CLI sends fanet1 (via fabric send) → app's lib repository can't decode. That's a real interop hole between two first-party surfaces introduced/extended by this very PR. I'm fairly confident this is a genuine finding.

However, severity calibration: the PR claims live verification "private channel messages decrypted in both directions between a headless DAP agent and the Flutter app". If that was true live, maybe the app-to-app DAP path uses... hmm, maybe when the app is a DAP member, the headless agent sends to it via DM (not channel)? "private channel messages decrypted in both directions" — channel messages. So either the live test ran over the fa_network path (EnvelopeCodec, which handles fanet1) or the claim is overstated. Either way the lib repository gap stands as code I read.

Let me now also check the receive path in lib for the app: does the app actually drain '#channel' inboxes? FallbackMessagingRepository primary = hub (lib repository) — peek/drain(agentId) — the lib repo's `drain` returns the whole `_inbox` regardless of the agent arg (peek/drain ignore the agentId per its doc). And `_onChannelMsg` adds channel messages to `_inbox`. So the app's DAP channel chat does receive channel messages that decrypt. fanet1 ones get dropped. Confirmed.

OK. Now let me also quickly check `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_network_transport_web.dart` (146 new lines) for the `?token=` bearer in web — the secret in a URL query param can leak via server logs/refer, but it's the hub's documented browser equivalent; hub_transport.dart warns "never log it". Check the web transport doesn't log the URL.

🚨 **BLOCKING: DAP env secrets are never registered with the redaction pipeline (ticket AC8/AC14)**

The ticket is explicit: *"CI test: the env values never appear in any session JSONL/tool result (**redactor registered for them**, the `SessionKeysStore` pattern)"* (`input/gh-1825/ticket.md`, Security & secrets). This PR adds the env contract (`DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` with **plaintext** `priv`s, `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`) but never registers those values anywhere. I grepped the whole diff: no `registerSecret` / `buildSecretRedactor` / redaction-pipeline touch.

Concretely: those variables live in the real process env (CI sets them there), so **every bash child inherits them**. A single `env` / `printenv DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` / `echo $DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` tool call puts plaintext channel private keys and hub credentials into the tool result → the session JSONL and the model context, unmasked. The L9 entropy layer is not a substitute: base64 with standard-alphabet `/` splits into tokens below the entropy gate, and human-memorable passphrases / short hub secrets fail Shannon heuristics by construction. There is also no test covering this (the AC8 "CI test" does not exist in `test/`).

Fix: register `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON`, `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` (and the decrypted privs / auto-provisioned passphrases held in `_memoryOnlyKeys`/`_memoryOnlySecrets`) into `RedactionPipeline.registerSecret` at startup (same pattern as `buildSecretRedactor` in `lib/src/cli/startup.dart:1054`), plus a byte-scan test that these values never appear in a session JSONL or tool result.

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the pure-Dart hub repository cannot open `fanet1` frames — the app DAP path drops private-channel mail the CLI fabric now sends**

The same PR makes the CLI fabric send private channel frames as `fanet1` (`bin/hub_fabric_repository.dart:147` → `client.sendChannelFanet1(...)`), and the CHANGELOG announces *"Inbound channel frames open `fanet1` first and fall back to legacy `dap/1` payloads"*. But that inbound open exists only in the vendored `fa_hub_client` 0.2.11 — **not here**. The Flutter app cannot import that package (its barrel pulls `dart:io`, per `flutter_app/lib/network/envelope_codec.dart:19` doc), so its DAP membership rides THIS repository (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_network_controller.dart:226`), and `_onChannelMsg` (this file, line 532) only understands:

- keyless → `_decodePublicChannelPayload`, or
- keyed → `hubDecryptPayloadWithKeyPair` expecting the **raw dap1 layout** `base64(nonce(12) || ct || tag)` with the sender key from whois.

A `fanet1` payload is `base64(0x01 || spk(32) || nonce(12) || ct || tag(16))` (`flutter_app/lib/network/envelope_codec.dart:30-36`). Decoding it as dap1 takes `nonce = raw[0..12)` = `0x01 || spk[0..11]` → AEAD tag mismatch → the frame is dropped at line 572 (`dropped undecryptable channel mail`). Result: an app enrolled via the DAP path (`dap_enrollment_service`) never receives private-channel messages from CLI/fabric agents, in exactly the interop scenario this PR headlines. The app's fa_network path handles `fanet1` via `EnvelopeCodec`; this repository needs the equivalent open (detect `data[0] == 1 && data.length >= 61`, extract `spk`, skip the 33-byte header before the AEAD) plus a round-trip test against `EnvelopeCodec.encrypt`.

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: undecryptable private memberships are classified as PUBLIC — the fabric then sends plaintext into a private channel**

`_isPublicMembership` decides the wire format from the **runtime-decrypted** membership: `membership.pub == null || membership.priv == null` → "public". But `DapScopedMemberships.runtimeEffective()` (`bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:465`) yields `priv: null` whenever the stored `dapkey1.` envelope could not be decrypted (missing passphrase — loud warning, "joined without keys, primary job proceeds"). For a PRIVATE channel that means: `pub != null`, `priv == null` → this check returns **true** → `HubFabricRepository.send` (`bin/hub_fabric_repository.dart:131`) takes the public-showcase branch and emits `base64({"text": …})` — **no encryption at all** — into a channel whose trust model is E2E ("the hub never sees plaintext", `_aboutText` in this file).

So one environment failure (no `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`, no Keychain hit) silently downgrades every outbound channel message from that agent to hub-readable plaintext, and keyed members render "(unable to decrypt)". The public/private decision must come from the **stored** membership shape (a truly public channel has `pub == null` at rest; a stored envelope or plaintext `priv` means private), not from runtime decryption success — and when the key genuinely cannot be resolved, the send should refuse/queue with a loud error rather than downgrade.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: unbounded PBKDF2 iteration count from the envelope — DoS via committed config or env**

`iterations` is read straight out of the (attacker-influenceable) envelope JSON with no sanity bound, then fed to `Pbkdf2(iterations: …)`. A `.fah/dap.json` committed to a repo someone clones (the ticket's v3 stance is that this file MAY be committed and team-shared), or a `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` env entry, can carry `"iter": 1000000000` — with `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` set (CI always has it), boot pays ~hours of KDF per envelope before the AEAD tag check ever runs. The format stores the count as data specifically so tests can lower it; it needs an upper bound too (e.g. reject `iter > 5_000_000` with the existing `FormatException` path, which already surfaces one clear warning and proceeds with the primary job). Cheap fix, closes a real boot-DoS slot.

## Automated Code Review — BLOCK

**Summary**: The scoped-join architecture, passphrase chain, and tests are strong, but three security/correctness findings must land before merge: (1) the new `DAP_*` env secrets are never registered with the redaction pipeline, so plaintext channel keys/hub credentials can ride `env` tool results into session JSONL (ticket AC8/AC14 requires the redactor registration explicitly); (2) the pure-Dart `HubMessagingRepository` — the only hub path the Flutter app can use — cannot open `fanet1` frames that this PR's own CLI fabric now sends, so app-side DAP channel mail from CLI agents is silently dropped; (3) a private membership whose key fails to decrypt is misclassified as PUBLIC and the fabric then sends unencrypted payloads into a private channel.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 DAP env secrets (`DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` plaintext privs, `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`) absent from `buildSecretRedactor` — no masking, no AC8 byte-scan test (comment1).
- 🚨 `fanet1` inbound gap in `lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart` (comment2); 🚨 silent E2E→plaintext downgrade via `_isPublicMembership` (comment3).
- ⚠️ Unbounded PBKDF2 `iter` from envelope (comment4); ⚠️ `parseDapEnvChannels` TypeError on wrong-typed `pub`/`priv` escapes warn-and-skip (comment5); ⚠️ plaintext-key overlay file never cleaned (comment6); ⚠️ global-scope join writes plaintext `priv`, contradicting the ticket's encrypted-global table — confirm vs ticket (comment7).
- ⚠️ (general, not inline) This repo's `.gitignore` ignores `.fah/*` except a whitelist that omits `dap.json`, so the "committable `.fah/dap.json`" path (AC14) and the dogfooded ai-teammate flow (AC12) cannot work in THIS repo — whitelist `!.fah/dap.json` or document the force-add.
- 💡 `_loadProject` drops all project memberships on one bad record (comment8).

**Next Steps**:
1. Register the DAP env secrets (and in-memory privs/passphrases) with `RedactionPipeline.registerSecret` + add the AC8 byte-scan test.
2. Add `fanet1`-first decode (with dap1 fallback) to the pure-Dart repository; round-trip test against `EnvelopeCodec`.
3. Base the public/private send decision on the stored membership shape; refuse/queue sends when the channel key is unresolvable.
4. Cap `iter`, make env parsing type-tolerant, clean up the overlay, decide the global-plaintext stance, whitelist `.fah/dap.json`.

All outputs are written and verified. Final review summary:

## Review of PR #1888 (gh-1825) — Verdict: **BLOCK**

Reviewed the full branch (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`, 109 files, +12615/-634), focusing on the security core: `dapkey1` envelope, scoped membership stores, passphrase→Keychain chain, `DAP_*` env contract, hub transports, fanet1 interop, and the app's DAP enrollment path. Findings (all anchored to added diff lines, machine-verified):

**🚨 Blocking (3)**
1. **Redaction gap** — `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` (plaintext privs), `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` are never registered with the redaction pipeline; the ticket (AC8/AC14) explicitly requires "redactor registered for them, the SessionKeysStore pattern". Any `env`/`printenv` tool result carries plaintext keys into session JSONL. No AC8 byte-scan test exists.
2. **fanet1 inbound gap** — the CLI fabric now *sends* private channel frames as fanet1 (`sendChannelFanet1`), but the pure-Dart `HubMessagingRepository` (the only hub path the Flutter app can use) only understands raw dap1 layout → the AEAD nonce lands on the wrong offset → app-side DAP channel mail from CLI agents is silently dropped, contradicting this PR's own CHANGELOG/live-verification claims.
3. **Silent E2E downgrade** — `_isPublicMembership` judges public/private from the *runtime-decrypted* priv; a private channel with an undecryptable envelope degrades to "public" and the fabric then sends unencrypted payloads into it.

**⚠️ Important (4)**: unbounded PBKDF2 `iter` from the envelope (boot-DoS via committed config/env); `parseDapEnvChannels` throws uncaught `TypeError` on wrong-typed `pub`/`priv` (verified live with dart, violates its own warn-and-skip contract); the plaintext-key runtime overlay `~/.dap/runtime/channels-$pid.json` is never deleted; global-scope join writes plaintext `priv` where the ticket's v3 table says encrypted (deviation question, cited).

**💡 Suggestion (1)**: `_loadProject` drops all project memberships on one malformed record. Plus a general-comment note: `.gitignore` doesn't whitelist `.fah/dap.json`, blocking the AC14/AC12 committed-config path in this repo.
